“—Well, being sick isn’t your fault. A cold this mild should pass if you take some medicine and sleep through the night, so stay quietly in bed.

“I’ll leave water on the chair. Try not to leave the detached room. Going outside will only chill you.”

As a precaution, I add another blanket and turn out the light.

“You can’t help catching a cold, right? You should be better by tomorrow if you drink some medicine and get a good night’s sleep.
I’ll leave some water here on the chair, so don’t go out of the building, okay? You’ll cool your body if you go outside.”
I put another blanket over her, just in case, and turn the lights off.

something tugs me back.

Then…

Her long hair hides her face, and I cannot see her expression.

…But her profile belongs to the painfully shy girl I met for the first time.
